title: Energizing Brazilian Rice-Syrup-Jocheong Agemono-Deep-Fry
description: A refreshing and energizing dish that combines the sweetness of rice syrup with the savory flavor of jocheong, all wrapped up in a crispy agemono batter. This Buddhist temple-friendly recipe is perfect for a quick and easy snack or light meal.
instructions: Combine rice syrup, jocheong, all-purpose flour, rice flour, and water in a large bowl to make the batter.
Whisk the batter until it's smooth and free of lumps.
Heat the vegetable oil in a deep frying pan or a deep fryer to 350°F (175°C).
Carefully drop the batter into the hot oil using a spoon, making sure not to overcrowd the pan.
Deep-fry the agemono for 2-3 minutes on each side, or until it's golden brown and crispy.
Drain the agemono on paper towels and sprinkle with chopped green onions, grated ginger, sesame oil, soy sauce, salt, and black pepper.
Serve the energizing Brazilian rice-syrup-jocheong agemono-deep-fry warm and enjoy!
Repeat the process with the remaining batter to make more agemono.
Serve the agemono hot with a side of steamed vegetables or a simple salad for a light and satisfying meal.
Store any leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 2 months.
When reheating, make sure the agemono is crispy by baking it in the oven at 375°F (190°C) for 5-7 minutes, or until heated through.
If desired, serve with a side of steamed rice or noodles for a more filling meal.
For a spicy kick, add some diced jalapeños or serrano peppers to the batter for an extra kick of heat.
To make the agemono more substantial, add some chopped cooked vegetables, such as zucchini or carrots, to the batter for added nutrition and flavor.
